title: Solana Generates 16.9 Times More Daily App Revenue Than Base (September 2026)
dek: Solana generated $5.14 million in 24-hour dApp revenue versus Base's $304,000 as of September 2026, according to DeFiLlama data cited by Crypto Briefing. Solana's monthly app revenue accelerated from $91 million in May to $143 million in August, roughly 57% growth.
author: Crypto Cronkite
key_fact: Solana's monolithic architecture is capturing app-layer monetization at 16.9 times the rate of Coinbase's Layer-2 Base, despite Base's low transaction costs and institutional backing.
bottom_line: The question is whether Solana's 57% monthly revenue acceleration from May to August sustains, or whether meme coin launchpad activity (identified as a primary revenue driver) contracts seasonally. A comparable May-to-August trend for Base, absent from this reporting, would clarify whether the 16.9x gap reflects structural Layer-1 advantage or cyclical app concentration on Solana.
body:
Solana generated $5.14 million in 24-hour dApp revenue versus Base's approximately $304,000, according to DeFiLlama data cited by Crypto Briefing. The 16.9-to-1 ratio reflects a widening gap despite Base's Coinbase backing and low transaction costs.
DeFiLlama's app revenue metric specifically tracks fees generated by decentralized applications such as DEXs, launchpads, and trading platforms, and deliberately excludes base-layer fees. Solana's revenue growth has been driven largely by trading platforms and token launchpads. Solana's high throughput has attracted a concentration of high-frequency trading apps and meme coin launchpads that generate substantial fees per user session.
Solana's monthly app revenue hit $91 million in May 2026 and climbed to $143 million by August 2026, an increase of roughly 57% over three months. Base has consistently ranked below Solana and other leading chains like Ethereum in daily app revenue. Base's transaction volumes have shown some activity at various points but the chain has not converted that activity into meaningful fee retention at the application layer. Base entered with strong backing from Coinbase and genuine excitement about Ethereum Layer-2 scaling, according to Crypto Briefing, yet well-known parentage and low transaction costs have not automatically translated into application-layer revenue.
